newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cattle ship sinking because of typhoon - AMLC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cattle ship sinking because of typhoon - AMLC.

text.p: The sinking of livestock carrier Guernsey Express in a typhoon off Guam on Sunday morning highlighted the power of nature rather than safety problems with the ship or the livestock trade, statutory authority Australian Meat and Livestock Corp said on Monday.

The Philippines-registered vessel, transporting 1,600 cattle from Brisbane to Osaka in Japan, took water and sank following a battering from 300 km an hour winds and 45 foot seas whipped up by Typhoon Dale, which caused extensive damage throughout the region, it said in a statement.
The 20 man crew spent six hours in a lifeboat before being rescued by the U.S. Coastguard 40 nautical miles southwest of Guam, it said.
AMLC general manager sheepmeat and livestock marketing Ralph Hood said the sinking was a regrettable "first" for the live cattle trade.
The trade had an impressive safety record and had never previously lost a ship, despite transporting almost three million cattle over the past 15 years, he said.

"While those groups opposing the export of live animals will undoubtedly claim the accident is the result of poor safety standards, I am sure that any reasonable person would accept that such extreme weather is beyond control," he said.
Hood stressed that the ship had been routinely inspected by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) before leaving port and was reportedly in good condition.

"It is important to realise that all livestock ships comply with AMSA standards which stipulate both the seaworthiness of the vessel and animal welfare requirements such as area, height, ventilation, light, feed and water," he said.
"While accidents such as this cannot be foreseen, the corporation works with the trade to ensure the safety and welfare of the animals is paramount," he said.
The 1,358 DWT Guernsey Express left Brisbane on October 29 for an expected 12-day voyage.
In 1995/96 Australia exported more than 627,000 head of cattle worth more than A$316 million, AMLC said.
While 80 percent of the exports were directed to Indonesia and the Philippines, exports of live cattle to Japan reached 9,944 during the same period, AMLC said.
The consignment of 1,600 head was worth about A$1.6 million.
